title: Supporting Local Entrepreneurs in Enhancing Sanitation - SEED Madagascar

facts.fact: The SEED blog post 'Supporting Local Entrepreneurs in Enhancing Sanitation in Southeast Madagascar' is dated 17 November 2021.
SEED, in partnership with UNICEF, is supporting local artisanal workers in building latrine platforms.
facts.quote: SEED, in partnership with UNICEF, is supporting local artisanal workers in building latrine platforms.

facts.fact: SEED's Rural WASH project uses a market-based strategy that aims to improve sanitation by creating a local market for sanitary goods in southeast Madagascar.
facts.quote: SEED has adopted a market-based strategy which aims to improve sanitation through the creation of a local market for sanitary goods in southeast Madagascar.

facts.fact: San Plats are mason-built sanitary platforms for household latrines, described by SEED as small concrete slabs with a tight-fitting lid.
facts.quote: mason-built sanitary platforms for household latrines (San Plats). These small concrete slabs can improve hygiene

facts.fact: SEED has begun focusing its activities on growing customer demand for sanitary products such as San Plats.
facts.quote: SEED has begun to focus its activities on growing the demand from customers for sanitary products like San Plats.
